clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 7945 is its operative paragraph, which further exempts Edward M. Weeks from compulsory retirement for age; the held text reads "for a period of one year ending August 31, 1939". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires that Edward M. Weeks, who had been exempted for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 7413 of July 10, 1936 and No. 7635 of June 16, 1937, be further exempted for a period of one year; the earlier exemptions are separate instruments that predate this one and cannot end it. The command is a one-person permission for a stated period, so it ended by its own terms on August 31, 1939; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day) under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md, and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. Later events recorded for this clause: Executive Order No. 8231 of August 31, 1939 grants a further exemption for a period of six months ending February 29, 1940 and recites this order among the earlier exemptions of Edward M. Weeks; it neither revokes nor alters the period stated in this order, and it is recorded as a later event, not as an end of this clause. A search of the held order texts for this order's number (jobs/claim-kit cruden search) finds it cited only in Executive Order No. 8231 (APP transcription and Photius printing of each), and the later order's own text grants a further period and leaves this order's stated period unchanged, so the stated date remains the first end under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on "further exempt" orders.

research_rationale:
EO 7945 (August 4, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt) is a one-person order exempting Edward M. Weeks from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, issued under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). This is the stale working-text recheck. The earlier claim quoted an American Presidency Project transcription; the working text is now the machine reading of the Government Printing Office printing held in jobs/mabillon-held-printings (grade machine_read_government_printed_copy, acceptable_as_original false; Executive_Orders_7262-8027.djvu; scanned pages 500-501; closing number tag 7945), and the Photius GPO printing of the same order (HathiTrust hvd.hl272j, jobs/photius-gpo-volumes/output/texts/EO_7945.txt) is also held. Standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. I read the working text in full and compared it word by word with the Photius printing and with the APP transcription: the number, date, title, signatory, authority citation, name of the person and the stated end date agree, and the only differences are OCR noise in the printings (garbled masthead and imprint lines, split or misread letters) that changes no number, date, signatory, name or period. The dateline in the working text reads "August 4, 1988" where the register, the printing and the APP transcription give August 4, 1938 (the year digits are misread; month and day agree). The APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names this order, its date agrees and its text_sha256 equals the held APP file. The Photius page-render check (jobs/photius-gpo-volumes/output/PAGE_CHECKS.csv) passes for this order: tag [No. 7945], dateline 1938-08-04, signatory Franklin D Roosevelt. The order is one recital paragraph and one operative paragraph (the text contains one "I hereby"), so the clause inventory is one whole-order clause. The operative words "for a period of one year ending August 31, 1939" fix the end of the exemption on August 31, 1939; that is the first end, recorded inclusive, with the exclusive reading disclosed. The packet's later-events and name searches each report 1 hit, and a search of the held order texts for this order's number finds it cited only in EO 8231; I read the held APP text of the later order and compared it with its Photius printing (only OCR differences), and I record it as a later event.
